abstract: We study the inverse problem of recovering algebraic cycles from moving period and apolar data on the Fermat sextic fourfold, whose rational Hodge conjecture is already known. Two disjoint Aoki--Shioda surfaces give a pencil of primitive classes with a uniform one-dimensional first-order Hodge excess. Exact second-order calculations separate the difference and sum classes: the chosen transverse difference direction is obstructed, whereas the sum direction extends through a finite formal Hodge jet of order six. The second-order transported apolar module has a unique quadratic generator transverse to the locus of split quadrics, together with four cubic generators modulo its multiples. The quadratic obstructs constructions requiring a split degree-two apolar generator but does not produce a cycle. Using the established complete-intersection period formula, we give a sufficient splitting criterion: a full apolar complete-intersection identity with the stated splitting and equation-membership hypotheses gives a $(2,3,3)$ surface representing the primitive functional. A fixed central union with the expected Hilbert polynomial has embedded Hilbert tangent dimension 116 and fails the incidence tangent equations for the chosen hypersurface direction. Standalone exact SageMath, Singular, and Python 3 verification scripts accompany these finite statements, with reruns of the second-order apolar and syzygy-separated Hilbert-tangent calculations. The results identify which geometric input is missing between a finite Hodge jet and an actual cycle. They neither prove an all-orders extension of the jet nor give a new case of the Hodge conjecture.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Section 2 (Proposition 2.1, addressing v1 review item 1): explicitly identified the 426-dimensional deformation slice as $R_6 = (S/J_F)_6$ ($\dim_K S_6 - \dim_K(J_F)_6 = \binom{11}{5} - 36 = 426$), recorded the explicit polynomial formulas for $P_0, H_0, H_1$ and the nine nontrivial simultaneous sparse quotient blocks of dimensions $4,8,23,12,8,18,24,18,8$, compared the rank drop inside the 23-dimensional block with Kloosterman's directed $61\times 61$ multiplication pairings [7, Construction 3.1, Lemma 3.13, and Theorem 1.6] (both dropping to rank 60), and explained via the Gauss--Manin relation on $F^3 H^4_{\mathrm{dR}}/F^4 H^4_{\mathrm{dR}}$ why vanishing of the 426 pole-two periods through order $s^N$ forces the holomorphic-form period to vanish through $O(s^{N+1})$.
- Section 3 (Theorem 3.1): wrote out the explicit Fermat Griffiths reduction operator $\mathcal{R}_{4\to 3}: S_{18} \to R_{12}$, the second-order Hodge equation (3.2) $M_P(H,q) = \frac{3}{2}\,\mathcal{T}_P(q,G,G)$, the self-pairing polynomial $\mathcal{T}_{P_t}(G_t,G_t,G_t) = \frac{5}{2}\mu^2 a\,t(t+1)$, and the explicit three-term kernel element $\kappa = x_2^2((1-\mu^2)x_3^4 + \mu^2 x_4^4 + x_5^4) \in \ker M_{P_{\mathrm{diff}}}$ that eliminates $H$ and the common kernel $K_0$ to block the entire non-common first-order coset $\alpha G_1 + K_0$ at $t=1$.
- Section 4 (Theorem 4.1, addressing v1 review item 2a): clarified that $(1,1,1)$ in degree two and $(10,10,10)$ in degree three are the dimensions of the central kernels in $S_r$ whose elements lift through the successive truncations modulo $s, s^2, s^3$ (whereas the full $K$-linear kernels of the $3\times 3$ block-Toeplitz systems have dimensions $3$ and $30$), and gave a self-contained algebraic proof via unique factorization and disjoint variable supports $\{x_0,x_1,x_2\}$ vs. $\{x_3,x_4,x_5\}$ that the split-quadric tangent space at $q(0)$ has dimension $11 < 12$ and $q(s)$ has symmetric rank $3+2=5$.
- Section 5 (Theorem 5.1, addressing v1 review item 2b): fixed an embedding $K \hookrightarrow \mathbf{C}$, defined $\mathfrak{m} = (x_0,\ldots,x_5) \subset S$, declared the nonzero generators $\bar{q} \in E_2$ and $\bar{r} \in E_4$ in Hypothesis 4 before writing $\gamma\bar{q}\bar{r} + Q$, explicitly set $g_0 = q$ in the proof of (5.2), and wrote out the degree partition $(\mathfrak{m}I^2)_6 = q^2 S_2 + q S_1 I_3$.
- Section 6, Reproducibility, and supplement (addressing v1 review item 3): wrote out the Hilbert polynomial $P_{Y_0}(d) = 9d^2 - 18d + 21$ ($d \ge 3$) and the degree-six expansion $H_{R/I_{Y_0}}(t) = 1 + 6t + 20t^2 + 48t^3 + 93t^4 + 156t^5 + 237t^6 + O(t^7)$ making the $847$ unknowns and $308 = 1+8+8+33+33+225$ zero-representative dimensions immediate; updated the text, abstract, and supplement (aoki-y0-hilbert-tangent.sage, syzygy-separated-verification.output.txt, apolar-hilbert-quotient-check.sage, verify_all_hodge41_claims.py, verify_all_hodge41_claims.output.txt, the supplement README, and CONTENTS.sha256) to record the full syzygy-separated rerun indexed by (syzygy_index, rdeg, target_e) over both $\mathbf{F}_{109}$ and $K$ ($1355$ equations, rank $423$, kernel $424$, tangent dimension $116$, incidence ranks $537/538$) and the standalone standard-library Python 3 verification script; and standardized the author line.

title: Moving Apolar Constraints on Hodge Cycles of the Fermat Sextic Fourfold
